summary: spectral-core 3.0.10 exfiltrates host files and environment to webhook.site at npm install via binding.gyp
details: The package ships a binding.gyp whose sole target has type 'none' and an inline `node -e` action that runs when npm triggers `node-gyp rebuild` on install. The action uses child_process.execSync to recursively list and cat files under /scripts, /opt, /root, and /home, dumps the full environment via `env | sort`, and POSTs the collected output over HTTPS to the hardcoded collector hostname webhook.site at path /f604623f-fc78-4447-9225-6772f7f12cb1. No C/C++ sources are shipped, so binding.gyp has no build purpose; the index.js entry is a 62-byte stub that only exports name and version, inconsistent with the package's self-described 'Spectral analysis core library' purpose. The harvested data includes SSH keys, cloud credentials,.npmrc tokens, and CI secret files commonly mounted under /scripts and /opt on build runners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
